# Court Cases Wrap-up

## By the end of today

You will be able to place speech, press, and civil-rights landmarks on the same map: courts defending a prior consensus against a current majority.

Speech is not unlimited. The fight is where the line is. *Brandenburg*: the state may punish speech directed to inciting imminent lawless action and likely to produce it. Advocacy of ugly ideas is not enough.

Prior restraint is the exception. *Tinker*: students do not shed constitutional rights at the schoolhouse gate.

*Plessy* to *Brown*: separate-but-equal was the 1896 settlement. Brown withdrew official school segregation. A movement still had work after the opinion.
